# Read and check the fitted survival regression

Use this sheet with [the R walkthrough](exercise-student.html). It shows the
same outputs when R access is unavailable. The regression
was fitted before class: these results do not require new inference.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(posterior)
library(bayesplot)
library(here)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 14))

ndd <- read_csv(here("data", "ndd.csv"))
fit <- readRDS(here("fits", "day2_ndd.rds"))
draws <- fit$draws
sampler_diagnostics <- fit$diagnostics
coef_draws <- posterior::subset_draws(draws, variable = c("alpha", "beta"))
stopifnot(
  fit$meta$stan_file == "stan/logit_reg.stan",
  nrow(ndd) == fit$data$N,
  all(ndd$n == fit$data$n),
  all(ndd$suv == fit$data$suv),
  isTRUE(all.equal(ndd$cons, fit$data$cons))
)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4.5
)
```

## 1. Trace plots

```{r trace-plots}
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(coef_draws, pars = c("alpha", "beta"))
```

Colours identify chains. They cover similar ranges without persistent drift or
separation. Next, check the numerical diagnostics.

## 2. Sampling diagnostics

```{r sampling-diagnostics}
sampling_table <- posterior::summarise_draws(
  coef_draws,
  rhat = posterior::rhat,
  ess_bulk = posterior::ess_bulk,
  ess_tail = posterior::ess_tail
)
knitr::kable(sampling_table, digits = 3)

# One row per chain, recorded when the model was fitted.
sampler_table <- as_tibble(sampler_diagnostics) |>
  mutate(chain = row_number(), .before = 1)
knitr::kable(sampler_table, digits = 3)
```

R-hat measures agreement across chains; values near 1 are encouraging.
ESS describes effective information in the draws: bulk ESS for the main part
of the posterior, tail ESS for its tails. It is not the seedling sample size.
Divergences signal potential sampling problems; investigate any nonzero count.
Read these together with the traces before interpreting coefficients. Successful
sampling does not establish ecological model adequacy.

## 3. Coefficient table

```{r coefficient-table}
coefficient_table <- posterior::summarise_draws(
  coef_draws,
  mean = mean,
  sd = sd,
  \(x) quantile(x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
)
knitr::kable(coefficient_table, digits = 3)
```

`mean` is the posterior mean; `sd` is posterior uncertainty; `2.5%` and
`97.5%` bound the 95% credible interval. Alpha and beta are on the logit scale.
The beta row is negative and its interval excludes zero: survival decreases
with density under this model.

## 4. Survival regression

```{r curve-probabilities}
density_grid <- tibble(
  cons = seq(min(ndd$cons), max(ndd$cons), length.out = 81)
)
curve_draws <- as_tibble(coef_draws) |>
  select(.draw, alpha, beta) |>
  crossing(density_grid) |>
  mutate(p = plogis(alpha + beta * cons))

curve_summary <- curve_draws |>
  group_by(cons) |>
  summarise(
    median = median(p),
    lower = quantile(p, 0.025),
    upper = quantile(p, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r regression-plot}
regression_plot <- ggplot(curve_summary, aes(x = cons)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "#d95f02", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median), colour = "#d95f02", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = ndd, aes(y = suv / n), alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Conspecific density (scaled)", y = "Survival probability")
regression_plot
```

Line: posterior median. Ribbon: 95% credible interval for survival probability.
Points: observed proportions. The curve shows lower survival at higher density;
the data, model, priors and draws stay fixed. The ribbon does not describe all
variation in future survivor counts. Making it darker changes only transparency.

Sampling diagnostics tell us about computation; they do not establish that the
ecological model is appropriate.
